name: Colón
shape: geoBoundaries, the department it is named for

climate: Seasons this warm ripen Cabernet Sauvignon, Sangiovese, Grenache, Carignan and Zinfandel fully without cooking off their freshness.
Cabernet Sauvignon sits in its sweet spot, so the wines can show the style it is known for.
Pinot Noir is at its warm limit. It can ripen too fast, giving heavy, soft wine that has lost its freshness.
Merlot is at its warm limit. It can ripen too fast, giving heavy, soft wine that has lost its freshness.
Malbec is at its warm limit. It can ripen too fast, giving heavy, soft wine that has lost its freshness.
Most rain falls while the vines grow. Damp leaves invite mildew and rot, so growers spray more and pick carefully.

soil.rock: Granite weathers to coarse, acid, free-draining soil that warms quickly and holds heat. Its acidity tends to lower the grapes' acidity, which suits Gamay. Schist, slate and gneiss break into stony, free-draining soil that holds the day's heat. Schist is rich in magnesium and potassium but poor in organic matter and nitrogen.
soil.top: The topsoil holds water well and drains at a steady pace, so vines rarely go thirsty or sit in wet ground. Its pH is close to neutral, so vines take up the nutrients they need easily.

land: The high ground runs about 8°F cooler than the low ground. Higher vineyards ripen later and keep more acidity, so one grape can make lighter or richer wine here depending on height.
Gentle slopes. Enough tilt to drain cold air and rain away, which lowers frost risk, yet still easy to farm by machine.

winkler: Good for generous crops of standard to good wine.
